_readme: Per-instance node notes: why THIS node exists in THIS workflow.
The note registry (docs-content, nodeLaymanDescriptions, nodeUsageGuides) already
explains what every node type does in general — that content is pulled in
automatically by extract-registry-notes.cjs and must NOT be duplicated here.
What the registry cannot know is why a particular node was placed in a particular
workflow, and what breaks if someone deletes it. That is what this file holds.
Keyed by template slug -> node id. Every node in ctrl_checks/templates/src must
have an entry; the contract test fails if one is missing.

approval-chance-predictor.form_details: Collects the exact details a verification reviewer checks, so the prediction is based on the same inputs a real reviewer would see.
approval-chance-predictor.airtable_lookup_readiness: Pulls this client's existing readiness record so the prediction builds on the earlier Readiness Checker result instead of starting from nothing. Filtered to one client — without the filter the AI would receive every client in your table.
approval-chance-predictor.ai_predict_chance: Compares the business against the reasons applications actually get rejected. It outputs one 'RISK:' line per problem found, which the next step counts.
approval-chance-predictor.js_percentage: Turns the AI's risk lines into a single number a client understands. Each risk costs 12 points off a 95% base — change those numbers here to make the estimate stricter or softer.
approval-chance-predictor.airtable_save_prediction: Writes the score back onto the same client row so the prediction is on file next time anyone opens the record.
approval-chance-predictor.slack_notify_team: Gives your verification team a heads-up on weak applications before the client chases them.
approval-chance-predictor.gmail_send_prediction: Sends the client their number. This is the deliverable — everything above exists to make this email accurate.

business-details-matcher.schedule_poll_clients: Runs the check on a timer because the platform has no 'Airtable row changed' trigger yet. Each run handles one client, so a 15-minute cycle clears a normal queue easily.
business-details-matcher.airtable_read_ready_clients: Picks up one client whose documents are complete and who has not been checked yet. The MatchCheckedAt filter is what stops the same client being re-reported forever.
business-details-matcher.js_detect_newly_ready: Lifts the selected client's name, website and email to the top level so the steps below can reference them directly.
business-details-matcher.if_hasclient: Most polls find nothing. Without this gate the workflow would fetch a blank URL and email an empty report every 15 minutes.
business-details-matcher.http_fetch_website_details: Fetches the live website so the AI can read the business details as they are published today, not as they were when the client signed up.
business-details-matcher.ai_extract_details: Reads the name, address and phone out of the website and each document, and returns them as JSON so the comparison below can be exact rather than a guess.
business-details-matcher.js_compare_versions: Compares every source field by field. This is where a mismatch is actually detected — the AI only extracts, it does not judge.
business-details-matcher.js_stamp_checked: Supplies the timestamp for the marker below. Needed because the platform has no {{$now}} built-in.
business-details-matcher.airtable_write_match_results: Records what matched and what did not, so the mismatch history lives on the client record rather than only in an email.
business-details-matcher.airtable_mark_checked: Stamps the client as checked. Delete this node and the same client is re-checked and re-emailed every 15 minutes, forever.
business-details-matcher.gmail_send_match_report: Tells the client exactly which detail is inconsistent and where — the specific thing that gets applications silently rejected.

client-priority-ranker.schedule_weekly_rank: Weekly is deliberate: this ranking is for planning the week's account-management time, not for reacting to events.
client-priority-ranker.airtable_read_client_history: Reads every client's delay and issue history — the ranking needs the whole set to rank them against each other. Capped at 200 rows so a large table cannot overflow the prompt.
client-priority-ranker.ai_estimate_outcomes: Judges which clients are drifting, using patterns a fixed rule would miss. Output format is one line per client so the next step can sort it.
client-priority-ranker.js_sort_by_priority: Sorts the AI's lines into a ranked list and formats it as text. Slack renders raw objects as unreadable JSON, so the formatting matters.
client-priority-ranker.slack_send_ranked_list: Puts the ranked list where the team already works. This is the whole output of the workflow.

cross-platform-sync-engine.schedule_poll_changes: Polls because there is no 'Airtable row changed' trigger. One record per run keeps the sync safe and rate-limit friendly.
cross-platform-sync-engine.airtable_read_all_clients: Picks up one record modified since it was last synced. The LastSyncedAt filter is the safety mechanism — without it every record looks changed on every run.
cross-platform-sync-engine.js_diff_changed_fields: Maps the Airtable row onto the shapes HubSpot and Sheets each expect. Your Airtable table needs a HubSpotId column for the CRM push to find the right contact.
cross-platform-sync-engine.if_hasrecord: Stops an empty poll from pushing a blank contact into your CRM and a blank row into your spreadsheet.
cross-platform-sync-engine.hubspot_push_changes: Updates the matching CRM contact. This is a write into your real CRM — test it against a sandbox contact before switching the template on.
cross-platform-sync-engine.sheets_update_shared_copy: Keeps the shared spreadsheet in step for people who do not have CRM access.
cross-platform-sync-engine.airtable_mark_synced: Stamps the row as synced. This is the single most important node here — remove it and the workflow re-pushes every client to HubSpot and Sheets every 15 minutes indefinitely.
cross-platform-sync-engine.slack_log_sync: A quiet audit trail so you can tell whether a sync ran without opening three systems.

customer-support-agent.chat_trigger_1: The customer's entry point. Everything downstream reads the message this produces.
customer-support-agent.memory_retrieve_1: Loads the last 10 messages so the customer is not asked to repeat themselves mid-conversation.
customer-support-agent.js_intent_1: Sorts the question into order / complaint / FAQ and pulls out an order ID if one is mentioned. Cheap keyword matching on purpose — an AI call per message would be slower and more expensive for no benefit.
customer-support-agent.switch_intent_1: Routes to one of three handlers. Only the matching branch runs.
customer-support-agent.db_order_lookup: Fetches the real order from your database so the reply quotes actual status and delivery dates rather than an AI guess.
customer-support-agent.js_format_order: Reduces the order row to the few fields the reply needs, and flags when nothing was found.
customer-support-agent.ai_order_response: Writes the customer-facing answer using the real order data supplied above.
customer-support-agent.ai_complaint_response: Handles complaints with an apology and a commitment, separately from factual queries — tone matters more than data here.
customer-support-agent.ai_faq_response: Answers general questions and offers a human when it does not know.
customer-support-agent.merge_responses: Brings the three branches back to one path so the confidence check and logging exist once rather than three times.
customer-support-agent.if_confidence_check: The safety gate. Confident answers go to the customer; anything below 0.75 goes to a human instead of guessing at them.
customer-support-agent.memory_store_1: Saves the exchange so the next message in the conversation has context.
customer-support-agent.log_output_1: Returns the final answer to the chat session.
customer-support-agent.db_escalate: Creates a support ticket so a low-confidence question is tracked and worked, rather than only pinged into Slack and lost.
customer-support-agent.slack_escalate: Pages a human with the original question and why the bot was unsure.
customer-support-agent.log_escalated: Records that this conversation went to a human — useful for measuring how often the bot defers.

document-vault-intake-auto-tagging.form_vault_upload: The intake point. A form is used rather than a watched Drive folder because the platform has no file-watch trigger yet.
document-vault-intake-auto-tagging.ai_tag_document: Reads the file and identifies what it is and what date it carries, so nobody has to tag documents by hand.
document-vault-intake-auto-tagging.js_parse_doc_tags: Turns the AI's JSON reply into real fields. Without this step the tags are written to Airtable blank.
document-vault-intake-auto-tagging.airtable_store_tagged_doc: Stores the file link with its tags. This table is what the Smart Search template reads — the two templates are a pair.

document-vault-smart-search.chat_trigger_search: Lets anyone ask for a document in plain English instead of digging through folders.
document-vault-smart-search.js_parse_search_query: Takes the raw chat message and prepares it as a search term. Written to work whether the chat trigger hands over a string or an object.
document-vault-smart-search.airtable_search_vault: Reads the tagged vault built by the Intake template. Capped so a large vault cannot overflow the agent's prompt.
document-vault-smart-search.ai_agent_find_match: Matches a loose human request ('that PAN card from March') against the tagged records and picks the best one.
document-vault-smart-search.whatsapp_reply_search: Returns the matched file link in the same chat where the request was made.

faq-answering-assistant.chat_trigger_faq: Lets clients ask their own questions instead of messaging your team.
faq-answering-assistant.airtable_read_faq: Loads your FAQ records. The AI answers only from these, which is what stops it inventing policy. Capped at 50 rows.
faq-answering-assistant.ai_answer_from_faq: Answers strictly from the supplied FAQ records and rates its own confidence, so the workflow can tell a solid answer from a guess.
faq-answering-assistant.js_parse_faq_answer: Extracts the answer and the confidence score from the AI's JSON. Without this the gate below has no confidence value to read and every question escalates.
faq-answering-assistant.if_confidence_check: Decides whether the client hears from the bot or from a person. 0.75 is the dial — lower it to answer more questions automatically, raise it to be more cautious.
faq-answering-assistant.whatsapp_reply_client: Returns a confident answer in the active chat session.
faq-answering-assistant.slack_escalate_human: Hands an uncertain question to your team with the AI's draft attached, so the human starts from something rather than nothing.

finance-compliance-agent.webhook_finance_1: Receives transactions from your accounting or expense system. This endpoint is currently open — put a shared secret in front of it before using real financial data.
finance-compliance-agent.js_extract_transaction: Normalises the many field names different finance systems use into one shape the rest of the workflow can rely on.
finance-compliance-agent.ai_categorize: Assigns a spend category. Doing this with AI rather than keyword rules is what handles vendors nobody has seen before.
finance-compliance-agent.js_parse_category: Extracts the category and confidence from the AI's JSON reply.
finance-compliance-agent.js_compliance_check: Applies your actual policy rules — amount ceiling, missing vendor, uncategorised spend. The approval threshold lives here; change it to match your policy.
finance-compliance-agent.if_compliant_check: Splits clean transactions from ones needing a human. Everything below exists on one side of this decision.
finance-compliance-agent.db_save_transaction: Records the approved transaction with its category, in your own finance database.
finance-compliance-agent.log_approved: A quiet trail of what passed, for reconciliation.
finance-compliance-agent.db_save_flag: Saves the flagged transaction with its violations attached, so the review queue is a real queue and not just a Slack message.
finance-compliance-agent.js_format_alert: Builds the human-readable alert and the machine-readable violations list used by the step above.
finance-compliance-agent.email_finance_alert: Emails the finance manager as well, because a Slack message at 6pm on Friday gets missed.

hr-hiring-workflow-agent.webhook_resume_1: Receives applications from your careers page or job board.
hr-hiring-workflow-agent.js_extract_resume_data: Normalises the varying field names applicant sources use.
hr-hiring-workflow-agent.ai_extract_skills: Pulls structured skills, years and education out of free-form resume text — the step that makes automated matching possible at all.
hr-hiring-workflow-agent.js_parse_skills: Converts the AI's JSON into real fields for the matching step.
hr-hiring-workflow-agent.ai_match_job: Scores the candidate against the role and explains its reasoning, so a human reviewing the decision can see why.
hr-hiring-workflow-agent.js_extract_match: Extracts the score and shortlist decision from the AI reply.
hr-hiring-workflow-agent.if_shortlist_check: The hiring decision point. 70 is the threshold, set in the matching prompt above.
hr-hiring-workflow-agent.db_shortlist: Records the shortlisted candidate. The candidates table must already exist with matching columns.
hr-hiring-workflow-agent.js_generate_calendar: Builds a personalised booking link. Replace the placeholder URL with your own scheduling link.
hr-hiring-workflow-agent.email_interview: Invites the candidate to book directly, removing the back-and-forth from scheduling.
hr-hiring-workflow-agent.db_reject: Records the decision and the reasoning behind it — needed if a rejection is ever questioned.
hr-hiring-workflow-agent.email_rejection: Sends a DRAFT rejection to your recruiter, not to the candidate. Automated rejections going straight out is a legal and brand risk; a person makes the final call here.
hr-hiring-workflow-agent.log_processing: Records every application processed, whatever the outcome.

internal-knowledge-ops-agent.js_prepare_query: Prepares the question and captures who asked. Written to work whether the chat trigger hands over a string or an object.
internal-knowledge-ops-agent.db_search_kb: Searches your knowledge base for articles matching the question. The ILIKE search on title and content is what makes the answer relevant — the previous version returned five arbitrary rows regardless of what was asked.
internal-knowledge-ops-agent.js_format_kb_results: Assembles the retrieved articles into one block for the AI and reports how much content was found, which the gate below tests.
internal-knowledge-ops-agent.if_kb_found: Decides whether there is enough material to answer from. Two separate conditions, because the runtime evaluates one comparison per row — a combined 'a && b' expression silently never matches.
internal-knowledge-ops-agent.ai_answer_with_sources: Answers from the retrieved articles and cites them, so an employee can verify rather than trust.
internal-knowledge-ops-agent.js_format_response: Appends the source list to the answer.
internal-knowledge-ops-agent.db_log_query: Records answered questions — the log that tells you what your team actually needs documented.
internal-knowledge-ops-agent.ai_fallback_answer: Says 'not in the knowledge base' politely and points elsewhere, instead of the AI inventing an answer.
internal-knowledge-ops-agent.db_log_not_found: Records the gap. Over time this becomes your documentation backlog.
internal-knowledge-ops-agent.slack_escalate_kb: Tells the knowledge team a question could not be answered so the gap gets filled.
internal-knowledge-ops-agent.merge_responses_kb: Brings both branches back together so the reply is returned once.
internal-knowledge-ops-agent.log_output_kb: Returns the final answer to the employee.

license-renewal-reminder.schedule_daily_check: Runs every 10 minutes and handles one licence per run, which clears any realistic renewal queue within the day.
license-renewal-reminder.airtable_read_expiry_dates: Picks up one licence approaching expiry that has not been reminded at its current milestone.
license-renewal-reminder.js_flag_expiring: Works out how many days remain and which milestone band the licence is in. The 90 / 30 / 7 day bands are set here.
license-renewal-reminder.if_shouldremind: Most runs find nothing. Without this the workflow would send a blank email on every empty poll.
license-renewal-reminder.airtable_mark_reminded: Records which milestone was sent. Delete this and the client receives the same reminder every 10 minutes until the licence expires.
license-renewal-reminder.gmail_send_backup_reminder: Emails the client at the right milestone. This is the deliverable, and the marker above prevents repeat reminders.

live-status-lookup-bot.chat_trigger_status: Lets anyone check a client's status without opening Airtable or asking a colleague.
live-status-lookup-bot.js_parse_lookup: Takes the raw chat message as the search term. Written to work whether the chat trigger hands over a string or an object.
live-status-lookup-bot.airtable_lookup_status: Finds the matching client. The name filter is essential — without it the bot returns the same first row no matter what was asked.
live-status-lookup-bot.js_format_reply: Turns the record into a readable sentence, and says so plainly when nothing matched instead of returning a half-empty status line.
live-status-lookup-bot.slack_send_status_reply: Replies in the channel where the question was asked.

missing-document-finder.form_doc_upload: Lets a client upload whatever they have, in any order. The client type chosen here decides which checklist applies.
missing-document-finder.ai_classify_document: Identifies what each uploaded file actually is, so clients do not have to label anything correctly.
missing-document-finder.airtable_log_document: Records the document against the client, building the running history the check below depends on.
missing-document-finder.airtable_read_prior_docs: Reads everything this client has ever sent. Without this the checklist only sees the file just uploaded and reports almost everything as missing.
missing-document-finder.js_check_missing: Compares the full set received against the required checklist. The two checklists — Individual and Business — are defined here.
missing-document-finder.ai_write_missing_message: Writes a short, friendly chase message rather than a blunt system list.
missing-document-finder.whatsapp_send_missing: Emails the client exactly what is still outstanding, which is what stops the back-and-forth.

new-client-risk-checker.form_new_client: The signup point, and the source of the domain that gets checked below.
new-client-risk-checker.http_domain_age_lookup: Looks up how long the domain has existed. A domain registered last week is one of the strongest fraud signals available. Needs your own WHOIS API key — replace the placeholder.
new-client-risk-checker.ai_risk_summary: Weighs the domain age together with the business name and site, and ends with a clear risk level.
new-client-risk-checker.js_risk_score: Converts the risk level to a number and applies your threshold. 80 is where compliance gets involved — change it here.
new-client-risk-checker.airtable_log_risk: Records the assessment on the client record so onboarding decisions are auditable.
new-client-risk-checker.if_high_risk: Only high-risk signups interrupt anyone. Everything else onboards silently.
new-client-risk-checker.slack_alert_compliance: Puts a risky signup in front of compliance before onboarding continues.

overdue-task-tracker.schedule_hourly_check: Runs every 5 minutes, handling one overdue request per run so a backlog clears quickly.
overdue-task-tracker.airtable_read_open_requests: Picks up one open request that is either unalerted or last alerted more than 4 hours ago — that window is what stops the same request pinging someone hourly forever.
overdue-task-tracker.js_flag_overdue: Compares how long the request has been open against its SLA and works out whether it is overdue or very overdue. Owner and manager channels come from the request row.
overdue-task-tracker.if_isoverdue: Most polls find nothing overdue. Without this the workflow posted a blank Slack alert every 5 minutes.
overdue-task-tracker.slack_alert_owner: Tells the person responsible, in their own channel, before the client notices.
overdue-task-tracker.airtable_mark_alerted: Stamps the alert time, which is what makes the 4-hour re-alert window work.
overdue-task-tracker.if_very_overdue: Separates 'late' from 'badly late'. Only the second one involves a manager.
overdue-task-tracker.slack_escalate_manager: Escalates when something has gone past twice its SLA and still nobody has acted.

sales-lead-qualification-agent.webhook_lead_1: Receives leads from your website forms or ad landing pages.
sales-lead-qualification-agent.js_extract_lead: Normalises the different field names lead sources use into one shape.
sales-lead-qualification-agent.ai_score_lead: Scores fit and intent from the lead's own details. The lead data is interpolated into the prompt — without that the model would be scoring nothing.
sales-lead-qualification-agent.js_extract_score: Extracts the score and qualified flag from the AI's JSON.
sales-lead-qualification-agent.if_qualified_check: Splits leads worth a salesperson's time from ones that get nurtured. 60 is the threshold, set in the scoring prompt.
sales-lead-qualification-agent.db_create_crm: Creates the contact in HubSpot so a qualified lead lands in your real CRM pipeline, not in a side table nobody works from.
sales-lead-qualification-agent.js_generate_booking: Builds a personalised booking link. Replace the placeholder URL with your own scheduling link.
sales-lead-qualification-agent.email_qualified: Invites a qualified lead to book while their interest is still fresh — the speed here is most of the value.
sales-lead-qualification-agent.email_followup: Keeps unqualified leads warm rather than dropping them.
sales-lead-qualification-agent.log_result: Records every lead and its score, which is how you tune the threshold over time.

smart-alert-co-pilot.schedule_poll_alerts: Polls every 10 minutes because there is no 'row changed' trigger. One record per run.
smart-alert-co-pilot.airtable_read_all_records: Picks up one record modified since it was last examined.
smart-alert-co-pilot.js_diff_for_alerts: Prepares the changed record for the AI to judge.
smart-alert-co-pilot.if_hasrecord: Stops an empty poll from burning an AI call and sending a blank alert.
smart-alert-co-pilot.ai_agent_judge_alert: The judgment layer, and the reason this template exists: it decides whether a change is worth interrupting a person for, rather than alerting on everything.
smart-alert-co-pilot.js_parse_alert_decision: Extracts the verdict, reason and severity from the agent's reply.
smart-alert-co-pilot.airtable_mark_alert_checked: Stamps the record as examined — deliberately BEFORE the gate below, so records judged not worth alerting are not re-judged and re-billed on every subsequent poll.
smart-alert-co-pilot.if_alert_worthy: Enforces the agent's verdict. Without this node the workflow alerts on every change and becomes a noisier version of a dumb alert.
smart-alert-co-pilot.js_route_notification: Sends high-severity alerts to the compliance channel and everything else to the account-management channel. Set both channels here.
smart-alert-co-pilot.whatsapp_send_smart_alert: Posts the alert to the one Slack channel that needs it.

submission-package-builder.schedule_poll_ready: Polls for clients who have cleared the readiness bar. One client per run.
submission-package-builder.airtable_read_ready_status: Picks up one ready client whose package has not been built yet.
submission-package-builder.js_detect_newly_ready_status: Lifts the client's website, name and email to the top level for the steps below.
submission-package-builder.if_hasclient: Most polls find nothing. Without this the workflow screenshotted a blank URL and emailed an empty package every 15 minutes.
submission-package-builder.http_screenshot_pages: Captures the homepage and policy pages as images, which verification submissions usually require as evidence. Needs your own screenshot API key — replace the placeholder.
submission-package-builder.http_fetch_policy_text: Pulls the live privacy policy and terms text so the submission quotes what is actually published today.
submission-package-builder.merge_package: Joins the screenshot and policy-text branches. Without this join the email could only ever see one of the two.
submission-package-builder.drive_list_existing_docs: Collects the documents already on file so the package is complete rather than partial.
submission-package-builder.airtable_mark_package_sent: Stamps the client as packaged so the same package is not rebuilt and re-emailed every 15 minutes.
submission-package-builder.gmail_send_package: Delivers every piece needed for the submission in one email. Pieces are sent as separate links because the platform has no PDF-merge step.

verification-co-pilot-chat.chat_trigger_copilot: Lets staff or clients ask about a client's status in plain English, from the chat tool they already use.
verification-co-pilot-chat.js_parse_query: Pulls the client name out of a conversational question. The pattern matching is deliberately simple — adjust it to your naming conventions.
verification-co-pilot-chat.airtable_lookup_client_record: Fetches the live record. Filtered by name so the agent receives the relevant client rather than your whole table.
verification-co-pilot-chat.ai_agent_answer: Answers only from the record it was handed, and says so when the data does not cover the question. That grounding is what makes the answer trustworthy.
verification-co-pilot-chat.whatsapp_reply_copilot: Returns the answer in chat, so nobody has to open Airtable.

verification-readiness-checker.form_intake: Collects everything the readiness check needs in one pass — details and documents together, so the client is not chased twice.
verification-readiness-checker.airtable_create_client: Creates the client record up front, so the score written later attaches to a row that already exists.
verification-readiness-checker.http_fetch_website: Fetches the client's live site so the AI can look for the pages verifiers check. If a site blocks automated requests this returns empty and the score will be misleadingly low — check the execution log before trusting a bad score.
verification-readiness-checker.ai_analyze_readiness: Checks the site and documents against what verifiers actually look for: privacy policy, terms, matching business details, working contact page. One 'ISSUE:' line per problem.
verification-readiness-checker.js_score: Turns the issue list into a 0-100 score. Each issue costs 15 points — change that here to make the score stricter.
verification-readiness-checker.airtable_update_score: Writes the score back onto the client record so it is on file for the next check.
verification-readiness-checker.ai_fix_list: Converts the technical issues into two or three plain-English actions the client can actually carry out.
verification-readiness-checker.js_compose_results: Assembles the score, fix list and contact details into one payload so the email has everything it needs.
verification-readiness-checker.gmail_send_results: Sends the score and the fix list. This is the deliverable the client came for.

patient-intake-triage.form_patient_intake: Collects the minimum structured details a clinic needs before deciding who should respond.
patient-intake-triage.ai_classify_triage: Turns free-text symptoms into a simple urgency decision that downstream routing can use.
patient-intake-triage.js_parse_triage: Converts the AI response into real fields so the branch below is deterministic.
patient-intake-triage.if_urgent_triage: Separates patients needing staff attention now from those safe for normal follow-up.
patient-intake-triage.slack_alert_clinic: Puts urgent cases where staff see them immediately.
patient-intake-triage.gmail_confirm_patient: Gives routine patients a clear acknowledgment and next step without waiting for a phone call.
patient-intake-triage.mongo_archive_patient_intake: Stores the structured intake and triage decision as a flexible clinical-admin document without changing the Slack or email routing path.

clinic-appointment-reminder.schedule_appointment_check: Runs daily because appointment reminders are time-based, not manually triggered.
clinic-appointment-reminder.airtable_read_appointment: Selects one appointment that still needs a reminder so each run is safe and repeatable.
clinic-appointment-reminder.js_prepare_appointment: Lifts the appointment row into fields used by the email and marker nodes.
clinic-appointment-reminder.if_has_appointment: Stops empty daily checks from sending blank reminders.
clinic-appointment-reminder.gmail_send_appointment: Delivers the reminder through Gmail, a verified working channel.
clinic-appointment-reminder.airtable_mark_appointment: Prevents the same appointment reminder being sent again on the next scheduled run.

lab-report-follow-up.form_lab_report: Collects the report summary and patient contact in one controlled intake.
lab-report-follow-up.ai_review_lab: Classifies whether the clinic team should review before a patient message goes out.
lab-report-follow-up.js_parse_lab: Makes the clinician-review flag available to the branch.
lab-report-follow-up.if_lab_needs_review: Keeps sensitive or unclear report follow-ups with staff instead of auto-emailing them.
lab-report-follow-up.slack_lab_review: Routes clinician-needed cases to the care team for human review.
lab-report-follow-up.gmail_lab_followup: Sends clear next-step communication when staff review is not required.

insurance-pre-authorization-tracker.schedule_preauth_check: Pre-authorization status changes are periodic, so polling is safer than manual checking.
insurance-pre-authorization-tracker.airtable_read_preauth: Handles one pending request per run to avoid duplicate notifications.
insurance-pre-authorization-tracker.js_prepare_preauth: Normalises the pre-authorization row into the status and routing fields used below.
insurance-pre-authorization-tracker.if_has_preauth: Stops empty polls from creating noise.
insurance-pre-authorization-tracker.if_preauth_staff: Separates requests that need staff intervention from simple patient updates.
insurance-pre-authorization-tracker.slack_preauth_staff: Gets denied or information-needed cases in front of the insurance desk.
insurance-pre-authorization-tracker.gmail_preauth_patient: Keeps patients informed when the request does not need immediate staff action.
insurance-pre-authorization-tracker.airtable_mark_preauth: Marks the request so it is not processed repeatedly.

patient-feedback-classifier.form_patient_feedback: Provides a simple channel for structured patient feedback.
patient-feedback-classifier.ai_classify_feedback: Turns free-text feedback into category and review fields.
patient-feedback-classifier.js_parse_feedback: Creates stable fields for storage and review routing.
patient-feedback-classifier.airtable_log_feedback: Keeps a searchable record of feedback themes and sentiment.
patient-feedback-classifier.if_feedback_review: Only interrupts staff when the classification says review is needed.
